correctness.rationale: For any connected nonnegative conductance vector, Kirchhoff index is (n+1)(tr(L+J)^−1−1). The Hessian along every nonzero edge variation is 2(n+1)tr(A² (L+J)^−1)>0, so unique global minimizer exists and wheel rotations force equal spokes a>0 and equal rims b≥0 without imposing symmetry a priori. Fourier modes yield (n+1)[1/((n+1)a)+sum_{k=1}^{n−1}1/(a+c_k b)], c_k=2−2cos(2pi k/n). Budget saturation n(Pa+Qb)=B yields scalar F=(P+Qz)S(z), z=b/a. S(0)=n²/(n+1), sum c_k=2n and sum c_k²=6n give derivative zero exactly Q/P=2(n+1)/n; strict convexity in budget-affine b gives unique activation and interior root. Second derivative and implicit Taylor yield stated local linear onset and quadratic improvement; Riemann-sum derivative limit gives z→max(0,P/Q−1/2), cost limit and critical window nz→max(0,(1−eta)/2) for Q=2P(1+eta/n). New checks computed independent weighted-Laplacian eigenspectra and derivative signs for n=3,4,7 and three price regimes (9 class parameter combinations). These finite checks do not establish general n/budget.
